# NASHA founder control center (generated by tools/founder_center.py; do not hand-edit)

**Readiness (from the scoreboard, unchanged by this page):** evidence 4/95, design 43/95. Nothing has been cooked, brewed, tasted, quoted, legally reviewed or tested with customers. Everything below is planning unless a row says otherwise; **digital progress is never physical evidence.**

**Two lanes.** Lane A needs the real world (cooking, brewing, tasting, customers, quotes, professionals). Lane B is autonomous digital work. A blocked Lane A item does not stop Lane B. Blockers are reported per workstream, not for the whole company.

**Top alert (D-78):** an Austin restaurant named Nasha was found by T1 searches: the name carries HIGH CONFLICT RISK until an IP attorney reviews it. `docs/decisions/DECISIONS.md` D-78; `brand/TRADEMARK-SCREENING.md`.

## Validation ladder (cheapest learning first; steps may be skipped)

| Step | Question answered | Cost | Speed | Reversibility | Lane | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V01 Founder kitchen prototype | Can the dish be made to a defined standard at all? | low | fast | high | A | Cut, rework or advance each dish |
| V02 Small blinded tasting | Do neutral tasters rate it intentional vs gimmicky? | low | fast | high | A | H2 first read; dish keep or cut |
| V03 Cultural review | Is the framing respectful, accurate and distinctive? | low | med | high | A | Brand and menu naming changes before public use |
| V04 Brewer review | Are beer concepts and pairings technically sound and feasible? | low | med | high | A | Pilot route and feasibility of Core 5 beers (F-3) |
| V05 Beer pilot | Can the Core 5 beers be made to target and sell? | med | slow | med | A | Beer thesis go or hold; G-6 sizing input |
| V06 Food x beer sensory session | Does pairing raise perceived value (H3)? | low | fast | high | A | Whether pairing is a core selling point |
| V07 Private invited tasting | Do invitees outside friends respond and give honest data? | low | med | high | A | Go or hold on paid testing |
| V08 Small paid tasting | Will strangers pay, and at what price? | low | med | high | A | H5 first read; pop-up go |
| V09 Brewery collaboration | Is there a willing licensed partner and workable terms? | low | slow | high | A | Partner path for residency and beer |
| V10 Brewery residency or pop-up | Do guests come and return in a real setting? | med | slow | high | A | Repeat-demand read (H10); trailer decision input |
| V11 Repeated paid events | Is demand consistent and economics positive across sessions? | med | slow | high | A | H7 unit economics read; investor-package data |
| V12 Commissary operation | Can prep run reliably at volume in a shared licensed kitchen? | med | med | high | A | H4 execution read; supply chain proof |
| V13 Food trailer | Does an owned unit improve access and margin over rented kitchens? | high | slow | med | A | Asset ownership go or no-go |
| V14 Small permanent operation | Do fixed-site economics and licensing work? | high | slow | low | A | Whether flagship should be larger or smaller |
| V15 Flagship | Does the full concept work at scale? | high | slow | low | A | Expansion consideration |
| V16 Desk validation (competitor, price survey,... | Which questions are worth testing physically? | low | fast | high | B | Sharper thresholds for V02-V08 |

## Capital allocation: do not spend flagship money to answer a small question

| Spend category | Prove first | Cheaper test first | Failure that saves the spend |
|---|---|---|---|
| PRODUCT R&D | Dish list frozen and sourcing check passed | Single-dish founder sessions (Chicken 65 Session 1) | Dish fails blind tasting; cut before more ingredients and trials |
| BRAND | Name legal view; cultural advisor feedback | Typographic placeholder only; no logo work (D-66) | Name not clearable or culturally problematic |
| LEGAL | Specific questions listed and scoped | Written question list (ATTORNEY-QUESTIONS), scoped engagement | Early attorney answer rules out a structure |
| BREWING | Legal route known; brewer engaged | Brewer review of recipes; partner-brewery pilot | Brewer or attorney says beer path unworkable |
| KITCHEN EQUIPMENT | Menu stable across repeated sessions | Rent time in a commissary or borrow equipment | Menu keeps changing; equipment would be idle |
| MOBILE MVP | Repeat demand at events; permit path verified | Pop-ups and brewery residency | Events show weak repeat demand |
| ARCHITECTURE | Site geography chosen; compact-site decision made | Concept diagrams only; no paid design | Pop-up and site learnings change the program |
| LEASE | Fixed-site economics and license structure proven | Residency as a rented site proxy | Residency data shows fixed site unjustified |
| BREWERY EQUIPMENT | Brewer sizing; beer demand proven by partner beer | Contract or collaboration brewing | Partner beer sells as well as would own brews |
| CONSTRUCTION | Licence in hand; costed design from professionals | Architect and cost consultant desk review | Quotes exceed what evidence can support |
| MARKETING | Product and message validated by real guests | Organic content, interviews, email list | Low organic response to tasting-stage product |

## Top risks

| # | Risk | Reduced by | Lane |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No physical evidence exists for any dish or beer | Cook Session 1 and the following sessions; a qualified brewer pilot | A |
| 2 | An Austin restaurant named Nasha (Indian Tex-Mex fusion with a bar) already exists per T1 searches: HIGH NAME-CONFLICT RISK (D-78) | IP attorney clearance review now; founder decision on keep/modify/fallback shortlist; no further name-dependent spend or public use until decided | A |
| 3 | No lawful structure may exist to link food and beer before a brewery exists (H11) | Texas alcohol attorney; commissary/health checks; food-only first tests | A |
| 4 | The fusion may read as gimmick or caricature (H2, H8) | Cultural advisor review; blinded tasting; dish-by-dish cut/rework rule | A |
| 5 | Unit economics are unknown (no price, yield, rent, labour, quote) | Real receipts and quotes; scenario model with provenance classes | A |
| 6 | Brewery scale and economics conflict with the building concept (50 bbl canon vs small demand) | Brewer-led sizing; pilot-first; do not size from renders | A |
| 7 | Customer demand and willingness to pay are untested (H1, H5, H10) | First-30 learning plan; thresholds frozen in advance; paid tests last | A |
| 8 | Kitchen bottleneck (comal and labour) and goat handling may limit the menu | Time real steps; cut or rework the weakest dish; operating-day requirements | A |
| 9 | Identity-critical ingredients (nixtamal tortillas, goat, paneer without bovine rennet) may be hard to source to specification | Supply-spec table; label checks; supplier declarations before any claim | A |
| 10 | AI-generated imagery and planning could be mistaken for evidence | Lane separation, stage labels, evidence audit, concept-only rule | B |
| 11 | Founder-dependence: one person running cooking, legal, research and outreach | Short review packages, prioritised queue, parallel workstreams | B |
| 12 | Responsible-alcohol and family-imagery missteps | Responsible-alcohol principles; image checklist; attorney and broker review | B |
